content.title: About
content.content: The chicken salad sandwich wrap is a soft wheat tortilla filled with a creamy chicken salad made from boiled chicken breast, mayonnaise, mustard, fresh vegetables, and aromatic herbs. It is a convenient, nutritious snack suitable for lunch, picnics, or a quick dinner.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken salad in the wrap is often mixed with celery and apple for a light sweetness and crunch.
The practice of wrapping salads in thin tortillas originated in the United States in the mid‑20th century as a fast take‑away option.
The tortilla usually contains a small amount of whole grains, boosting its fiber content.
Wraps are easy to cut into bite‑size portions, making them popular in catering.
Variations may replace mayonnaise with a yogurt‑based sauce to lower calories.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken breast provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken supplies niacin, vitamin B6 and B12, which support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Using light mayo or yogurt keeps saturated fat levels moderate.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Vegetables in the salad (e.g., carrots, celery) add dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Vitamin C from veggies
items.content: Fresh peppers and other vegetables boost the wrap with vitamin C, supporting immunity.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken or added ingredients.

items.title: Mayonnaise content
items.content: Traditional mayo increases calories and fat; light versions are recommended for weight‑watchers.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Chicken must be fully cooked and stored below 4 °C to prevent salmonella growth.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Prepared sauces and seasonings can be high in salt; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The wrap is easy to eat by hand, preferably cut in half. It can be served cold or gently warmed in a microwave. Pairs well with a light green salad or a fruit juice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the assembled wrap in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, separate the tortilla from the salad to prevent sogginess.
